Night both x
Night Tom x
Morning Jo, thanks. Post them when you've checked them. Night Tom x
Thanks Maya. I'll post them as soon as I've checked.
Thanks Jo.
I'm up now, so I'll try Dad this afternoon and let you know what he says.
Thanks Tom, let us know what he says.

Thanks Tom, let us know what Dad says. Maya, I still haven't posted the trains or the headcount, and I'm sorry for the delay. I'll get them sorted tonight and post them here before you ring any function rooms.
I'll let you know as soon as I've spoken to him, Maya.
No problem, Jo. Tonight's fine. Tom, thanks, I'll wait to hear from you.
Thanks Maya, I'll post the trains and headcount tonight.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Tom. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You three grew up in Hexham, Northumberland, where your parents still live, and now you're spread across Leeds, Edinburgh and Manchester, keeping in touch through a group chat that's mostly logistics and memes.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You live in Leeds and work as a pharmacist at a busy high-street branch, and this week you're covering three extra shifts while a colleague recovers from a broken wrist.
privateLines.Tom: You live in Edinburgh and work as a sound engineer at a repertory theatre, and this week you're tech-rehearsing a Stoppard revival that opens Friday, which means long nights at the mixing desk in the dark.
privateLines.Jo: You live in Manchester and teach secondary school geography, and this week your Year 10 coursework deadlines are piling up while your boiler has started making a noise you can't ignore.

turns.text: Hiya both. Shifts this week have fried my brain, so forgive the late message. Has either of you thought about Mum's 60th next month? Nobody's planned anything yet and I don't want it to slip. Could we pick a weekend and maybe split things up? I can sort a restaurant in Hexham if one of you handles the cake and the card?

Hiya Maya. Yes, I've been meaning to say something about it. Dec is nearly here. Restaurant in Hexham sounds good, and I'm happy to do the card and get everyone's names and messages in it. I'm drowning in Year 10 coursework this week and my boiler's making a racket, so I can't promise cake right now. @Tom, can you take that one? Weekend of 6th or 13th for the do?

Brilliant, thanks Jo. Card sounds perfect, and don't worry about the cake, I'll chase that up with Tom. I'm off shifts on the 6th so I'd say that weekend, but I'll check the restaurant has space before we lock it in. Tom, you about?

Yeah, I'm here, just buried in tech for the Stoppard opening on Friday. The 6th works for me. I'll take the cake: I can order one from a bakery in Hexham and collect it on the day, so if you give me the restaurant time and number of people I'll get the cake sorted. Maya, let us know once the restaurant confirms, and I'll look at trains from Edinburgh.

Great, Tom, cake's yours then. I'll ring the restaurant tomorrow after my shift and try for a table on the 6th around 7pm. Probably about 12 people if Auntie Sue and the cousins come, so I'll confirm the number once I know. I'll post here as soon as I've got an answer.

Brilliant, Maya, 7pm on the 6th sounds good. Ring me if the restaurant wants a deposit or the number changes. I'll sort the cake once you've confirmed the table, and I'll message Jo to check she's happy with the card plans. Hopefully the lot of us can get the train up on the Friday night.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning all. I'm at work from 8 so I'll ring the restaurant on my break around 1pm. Tom, I'll let you know about any deposit straight after. Friday night train works for me too, so I'll look at tickets from Leeds to Hexham once the table's booked.
Morning Maya, 1pm sounds good. Let me know about the deposit and I'll sort my share. I'll check the Edinburgh to Hexham trains for Friday night too. Good luck with the shift.
Thanks Tom! I'll let you know what the restaurant says at lunch. Off to work now, speak later.
Good luck at work, Maya. Speak later.
Cheers Tom. Speak later, Jo, and I'll update you both after lunch.

Morning both. Sounds like it's all coming together. Maya, thanks for ringing the restaurant at lunch. Tom, cake's yours, and I'll get the card round to everyone once I know the numbers. Hopefully my boiler holds out until the 6th.
Morning Jo! Just to be clear, I haven't rung the restaurant yet. I'm not on my break until 1pm, so I'll do it then and let you both know. Hope the boiler holds out.
Thanks Maya, I'd misread that. I'll wait for your update at lunch before I start on the card. Hope the shift goes alright.
Thanks Jo, I'll update you both at lunch. Hope Year 10 coursework doesn't eat your whole evening.
Cheers Maya. Coursework's going to eat my evening regardless, so I'll keep my head down and wait for your lunchtime news.
Will do, Jo. Thanks for sorting the card.

Morning both. Nice one, Maya, I'll wait to hear from you at lunch. Jo, thanks for doing the card. I'm at the desk for the Stoppard tech until late, so I'll sort the cake once we've got the table confirmed.
Morning Tom. I haven't actually started the card yet, I'm still waiting on Maya's update about the table. Good luck with the tech for Friday.
Cheers Jo, I'll wait for Maya's update too. Thanks for holding off on the card.
No bother, Tom. I'll wait for Maya's update at lunch and then get going on the card.
Sorry both, I got caught up on the ward and haven't rung yet. It's now 2:30 and I'm just about to ring the restaurant on my afternoon break. I'll post the result here as soon as I've spoken to them.
No worries, Maya. Let us know what they say when you get a minute.
Will do, Tom. Ringing them now.
No stress, Maya. Let us know what the restaurant says when you've got a minute. I'll hold off on the card until then.
Sounds good, Jo. I'll hold off on the cake until we hear back too.

Sorry, I've been putting this off and I should have just rung. I'm covering the till until close and the phone's behind the counter, so I'll ring the restaurant first thing tomorrow and post the result straight away. Jo, go ahead with the card in the meantime. Tom, hold the cake until I've confirmed.
No problem, Maya. Thanks for letting us know. I'll hold the cake until you've confirmed the table. Jo, go ahead with the card whenever you're ready.
Thanks Tom. I'll ring first thing tomorrow and post the result here as soon as I have it.
Sounds good, Maya. Speak tomorrow.
Speak tomorrow, Tom.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Morning both. The restaurant won't be open yet, so I'll ring when they open and post the result here.
Morning Maya. Sounds good, speak once you've got them on the phone.
Morning both. Thanks Maya, I'll start on the card now so it's ready once the table's sorted. Let us know what the restaurant says.
Morning Jo, thanks for getting going on the card. I'll sort the cake once Maya confirms the table.
Cheers Tom. Once Maya's confirmed the table I'll get everyone's names and messages collected for the card.
Sounds good, Jo.
Sounds good. I'll wait for Maya's call and go from there.
Morning both, sorry, it's lunchtime and I've only just got a minute. I'm ringing the restaurant now and will post what they say.
No problem Maya, thanks for chasing it. Let us know what they say.
I'm on the phone to them now. Will post the moment I know.
Thanks Maya, good luck on the call.

Thanks Jo, but I have to be straight with you both: I haven't actually rung yet. I said I was on the phone and I wasn't. I'm sorry for the runaround. I'll ring them properly now and post the result as soon as I have it.
No worries, Maya. Thanks for being honest. Ring them when you can and let us know. Take your time.
Thanks for being straight with us, Maya. Ring whenever you're free and let us know. Jo, I'll keep holding the cake until we have the table.
Thanks Tom. I'll keep the card on hold until Maya's got the table sorted. Maya, no pressure, just let us know when you've spoken to them.
Sounds good, Jo. Maya, just let us know when you've spoken to them.
Will do, Tom. I'll get on with my marking and keep an eye out for Maya's update.

I still haven't rung the restaurant, and I'm sorry I've kept you both waiting. I'll ring them tomorrow morning when they open, and I'll post what they say as soon as I know. If the 6th is still free, I'll try for a table then. If not, we'll pick another date and I'll tell you straight away.
Thanks for being straight with us, Maya. Ring them tomorrow when you can and let us know. If the 6th's gone, we'll just pick another weekend. Don't worry about it.
No stress, Maya. Ring them tomorrow and let us know. If the 6th's gone we'll pick another weekend, and I'll check the train times for whichever one it ends up being.
Thanks Tom, I'll ring them first thing tomorrow and let you both know.
Sounds good both. Speak tomorrow once Maya's been on the phone.
Sounds good, Jo. Speak tomorrow.
Night Tom. Speak tomorrow.
Night Jo.
Night Tom.
Night both. I'll ring first thing and post the result tomorrow.
Night Maya. Thanks for sorting it.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning both. The restaurant won't open until later, so I'll ring as soon as they do and post the result here.
Morning Maya. Sounds good, let us know once you've got them.
Will do, Tom.
Morning both. Maya, ring when they're open and let us know. Tom, I'll keep the card on hold until the table's confirmed.
Morning Jo. I'm starting my shift at 8 so I can't ring them until my break. I'll post the result as soon as I've spoken to them.
No worries, Maya. Ring them on your break and let us know how it goes.
Will do, Jo.
Thanks Maya.

I'm sorry, I still haven't rung them, and I need to be honest about why. I keep saying I will and then not doing it, and that's wasted your time. Can one of you ring the restaurant? I'll send the number and the 6th at 7pm for 12 people, and I'll ask Claude to check any online booking options if that's easier. Tell me which you'd prefer.

Thanks for being honest, Maya. I can ring the restaurant myself, but I'm at the desk for the Stoppard tech until late tonight. If you send me the number and the details, I'll ring first thing tomorrow, before the shift. Or I can check whether they take online bookings. Either way, I'll sort it and post the result here.

Thanks Tom. I have to admit I never picked a restaurant, so I don't have a name or number to send you. Could you pick one in Hexham that does a group of about 12 and check whether they have a table at 7pm on Saturday the 6th? If you'd rather I look up a shortlist first, I can do that and send it over tonight.
Right, I'll look into it. Asking Claude to find restaurants in Hexham that can seat about 12 on Saturday the 6th at 7pm, so I'll post what I find.

@claude Can you find restaurants in Hexham, Northumberland that take group bookings for about 12 people? I'm after a place that could seat a group on Saturday 6 December at 7pm. Please give me a shortlist with phone numbers, whether they take online bookings, and anything about group or private room options.

I found three Hexham restaurants worth ringing. I couldn't confirm that any of them has a table for 12 at 7pm on Saturday 6 December. Pages for the Boatside Inn and Vercelli wouldn't load when I tried to open them, so their details come from search results only.

**1. The Boatside Inn** (Warden, just outside Hexham)
- **Phone:** 01434 602233 (listed on several OpenTable pages).
- **Online booking:** It has an [OpenTable listing](https://www.opentable.co.uk/r/the-boatside-inn-hexham).
- **Group options:** It has a private dining room. Listings give the capacity as 25 or 26, and one says the whole restaurant can be booked for up to 50. It can plan menus from buffet to four courses. This is the strongest fit for 12.

**2. Vercelli** (36–38 Priestpopple, Hexham)
- **Phone:** 01434 603350.
- **Online booking:** It's on [OpenTable](https://opentable.co.uk/r/vercelli-restaurant-hexham). One listing says booking is by phone only, with payment (£45 a head) at booking. That may apply only to a special event or set menu, so ask when you call.
- **Group options:** An earlier search result mentioned a separate event space and a 50-seat banquet hall. I couldn't verify either.

**3. Bouchon Bistrot** (4–6 Gilesgate, Hexham NE46 3NJ)
- **Phone:** 01434 609943 ([SquareMeal](https://www.squaremeal.co.uk/restaurants/bouchon-bistrot-hexham_13381)).
- **Online booking:** SquareMeal takes requests for 1–14 people, but the restaurant has to confirm each one. It's also on OpenTable.
- **Group options:** [Cvent](https://www.cvent.com/venues/hexham/restaurant/bouchon-bistrot/venue-c02432b7-30b1-4232-995a-fa10def41ebd) says private dining is available but gives no capacity. Saturday dinner reportedly runs until about 9pm, so a 7pm start should fit, but confirm that.

**Other leads**
- **Slaley Hall** (just outside Hexham) has private Christmas party nights, reportedly from £39.95 a head. That price comes from a search snippet and may be out of date.
- The Beaumont Hotel appeared in a Living North private-dining article, but I couldn't confirm what it offers.

6 December is a peak Christmas weekend, so phone soon. Ask about deposits, pre-ordering and set menus for large groups, and whether you'd get a private room or just a table in the main dining room. Opening hours can change, so check them too.

Thanks both. Tom, I'll leave the restaurant search with you and Claude. Once you've got a shortlist, I can help pick one and sort the card.

Thanks Claude, that's really useful. The Boatside Inn looks like the best fit for a group of 12 with its private dining room. I'll ring them tomorrow morning before my shift, and I'll post what they say. If they don't have the 6th at 7pm, I'll try Bouchon Bistrot next.
Nice one Tom, the Boatside sounds like a good shout. Let us know what they say tomorrow, and if the 6th doesn't work, we'll try Bouchon next. I'll get names for the card in the meantime.
Cheers Jo, I'll ring the Boatside first thing and post what they say.
Cheers Tom. Speak tomorrow once you've rung them.
Speak tomorrow, Jo.
Speak tomorrow, Tom.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya, Jo and Sam. You work together at a small design studio. You all live within a few miles of each other in Leeds and met as students on a design course at the city's art college, and now you work together at a small studio in Hunslet.
topic: A client has just moved a deadline up to Friday.

privateLines.Maya: You are the studio's typographer, working from a converted shopfront in Kirkcaldy, Scotland, and this week you're halfway through a hospice charity's new signage system while your landlord keeps delaying the boiler repair.
privateLines.Tom: You handle print production from a flat above a launderette in Leeds, and this week your van has failed its MOT with a list of repairs you can't afford, so you're relying on lifts for the print runs.
privateLines.Jo: You are the studio's illustrator, working from a spare room in Shipley, and this week you're finishing a set of botanical drawings for a seed company while your toddler is teething and sleeping in short stretches.
privateLines.Sam: You run the studio's accounts from a back office in Hull, and this week you're reconciling a messy year-end ledger for a client who keeps sending receipts in shoeboxes, while your son sits his GCSE mocks.

turns.text: Hey all. Sunday evening and I'm still wrestling with the hospice signage grid. Client moved the deadline to Friday, so I'm not really relaxing. Anyone else got the Friday email, or is it just me?
Not me yet, Maya. Sorry the Friday deadline is landing on your Sunday. If the grid's giving you trouble, I can take a look at the print specs tomorrow morning before I'm on the press run.

Thanks, Tom, that's kind of you. Tomorrow morning would help. The grid's fine, really. My problem is the wayfinding icons don't sit right at the small sizes, and I haven't checked the minimum print size yet. If you can look at the spec sheet with me, that'd save me an hour of guessing. I'll send over the PDF tonight so you've got it before you start.

Sorry Maya, Friday's a rough one to get on a Sunday. I've been buried in a shoebox ledger from Hull all evening, so I'm no use for the spec sheet tonight. Tom's on it tomorrow, and I'll look at the icon sizing with you Monday if the grid's still giving you grief. Send the PDF over whenever. I'll have a look at it before bed if I get a minute.

Thanks, Sam. Don't worry about tonight, you've got enough on with that ledger. Tom's got the spec sheet tomorrow, and Monday works if the icons are still off. I'll send the PDF over now so it's waiting for both of you.

Sounds good, Maya. I'll look at the PDF first thing tomorrow. I'm without the van after the MOT, so I'll need a lift in, but I can still check the icon sizes before I'm at the press. Send it over when you're ready.
Thanks Tom. Sorry about the MOT. I can sort out a lift for you. I'll send the PDF over tonight so it's on your phone before the morning. If it doesn't come through, just ping me and I'll resend it.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning both. Tom, I should own something: I said I'd send the spec PDF last night, but it hasn't gone out. I'll send it as soon as I've got it in front of me. Still on for the lift? I can pick you up from yours if the bus is a faff.
Morning Maya. No stress about the PDF, these things happen on a Sunday. Tom's the one who needs it, so I'd send it as soon as you can.
I'm still at the ledger, so I can't help with the lift or the icons this morning. If the grid's still off on Monday, I can look at the wayfinding sizes with you then. Good luck with the day.
Morning, Maya. Thanks for the lift offer. Yes, please, that'd be great. Pick me up when suits you. I'll wait for the PDF, and I'll check it as soon as it lands.
Morning Sam, thanks. Tom, I'll get the lift sorted for you. I'll be leaving soon, so I'll message when I'm on my way. Sending the PDF now.
Thanks, Maya. I'll keep an eye out for the PDF and for you. Once I've got the spec sheet I'll check the icon sizes against the minimum print size before we get to the studio.

Tom, I need to correct myself. I said I was sending the PDF, but it hasn't gone through. Attachments aren't working on my end, so I can't send it from here. I'm sorry for the mix-up. Can you get the spec sheet from the client's brief or the shared folder? If not, tell me what you need from it and I'll type out the minimum print sizes and the icon measurements. I'm still happy to pick you up, so tell me when suits.

No problem, Maya. I'll check the shared folder and the client brief now. If the spec sheet's not there, I'll ask you to type out the minimum print sizes and icon measurements. Sorting the lift can wait until I know what I'm working from.

Sounds good, Tom. If the shared folder's a dead end, I'll pull the icon measurements and minimum sizes from my notes and type them out for you. Message me when you've checked, and we'll sort the lift after that.
Will do, Maya. I'll check the folder and message you what I find.

Morning all. Sorry Maya, that's a frustrating one with the attachment. Tom, if the shared folder's a dead end, I'm around between ledger batches, so I can help you sort out the minimum sizes against the brief if you message me what you find.
Thanks, Sam. I haven't checked the folder yet, so I'll let you know what I find. If it's a dead end, I'll take you up on that.
Sounds good, Tom. Message me whatever you find and I'll help you sort the sizes. I'm back on the ledger until lunch.
I need to be straight with you both: I haven't been able to check the shared folder, and I shouldn't have said I was going to. I can't reach it from here, so I'm still missing the spec sheet.
Maya, could you type out the minimum print sizes and icon measurements when you get a moment? Sam, if you're free after lunch, we can check them against the brief together.
Meanwhile, I'll ask Claude for general guidance on minimum icon sizes for wayfinding signs so we have a starting point.

@claude What are the usual minimum sizes and clearances for pictogram/wayfinding icons on printed signage, particularly for small sizes? Please cover UK guidance such as RNIB or BS 8300 where relevant, and say where a client brief would normally override general guidance.

Thanks for being straight about the folder, Tom. No need to apologise. Asking Claude for a starting point is a good idea. Maya's the one with the numbers, so once she's typed them out, I'll check them against the brief with you after lunch. Message me when you're ready.
Thanks, Sam. I'll message you once I've got Claude's answer and Maya's numbers. Maya, the measurements are still the bit we need from you.
Sounds good, Tom. I'm back on the ledger, but I'll check my messages once Maya's numbers are in. Message me when you're ready.

Tom, I don't have the exact figures in front of me, so I don't want to type out numbers I'm not sure of. The icon measurements and minimum print sizes are in my working file on the studio machine, and I can't reach that from my phone. I'll check it when I'm back at my desk and send you the exact values, not my memory of them. Your Claude question is a good idea too, since it'll give you general guidance to compare against the brief.
Good call, Maya. Better to wait for the exact values than work from memory. Tom, once Claude's answer and Maya's figures are in, message me and we'll check them against the brief.

Thanks, both. That makes sense, Maya. I'd rather wait for the exact figures than guess. I'll check Claude's answer when it comes back and let you know what it says. Maya, if you can send the values when you're at your desk, I'll compare them against the general guidance and then we can check everything with Sam.
Sounds like a plan, Tom. Once you have Claude's answer and Maya's values, send them over and I'll check them against the brief with you.

Sorry both, I haven't been able to get the figures yet. I'm not at my desk, so I can't open the design file, and I don't want to send values I haven't checked. I'll be in the studio tomorrow morning, and I'll send the exact numbers as soon as I'm there. That still leaves time before Friday. Tom, I'm also happy to sort the lift tomorrow, once you know your timings.
Thanks for flagging that, Maya. Tomorrow morning works, and Friday still gives us room. Tom, when you've got your timings, let me know and I'll help you sort the rest of the checks.
Thanks, Maya. Tomorrow morning works, and Friday still leaves room. I'll message you both once I know my timings for the lift. Sam, I'll bring you Claude's answer and Maya's numbers once they're in.

Thanks both. I'll be in the studio first thing tomorrow and will send the exact icon sizes and minimum print figures as soon as I've checked the file. Tom, message me your timings and I'll sort the lift.
Sounds good, both. Once the numbers are in, send them my way and I'll go through them with Tom against the brief.
Will do, Sam. I'll send them as soon as I've checked the file tomorrow.

topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You run the front desk at a veterinary clinic on the edge of town, and this week a retired greyhound you're fostering has refused to come out from under your sofa, so your evenings revolve around coaxing her out with chicken.

turns.text: Hiya both! Is anyone free for a catch-up sometime soon? Could do a pint or a brew at mine. Fair warning, the greyhound is still under the sofa, so you'll be meeting her from underneath. Let me know when you're free 🐾

Hiya Maya! Yeah, I'm keen. Cheers for the invite. Fair warning, my shifts flipped on Monday so I'm on early starts now and I don't know my days off for next month yet. Give me a day this week and I'll tell you if I can make it. Is the greyhound still under the sofa? Can't wait to meet her from down there 🐾

Hiya! I'm buried in parents' evening prep this week and the quilt for my sister's wedding is a race against December, so I'm a maybe for the weekend after. Can't wait to meet the greyhound from under the sofa 🐾

Sounds like a busy few weeks, Jo! The quilt for your sister's wedding sounds lovely. Let us know when you've got a free evening. I'll check my rota once the new shifts settle and say which days I can do. Maya, I'm free on the days that suit you best, so pick one and I'll try to fit it in.

Ha, she's still under there. I've been bribing her out with chicken and she's not impressed yet. @Jo no stress about the quilt, the weekend after is fine. @Tom, Thursday after footy or Wednesday? Tell me which suits and I'll pencil it in for everyone 😊

Brilliant, thanks Tom. I'll go with Thursday after footy, since that's the one we can all manage without a special trip. @Sam, you still around? Let us know if Thursday works. @Jo, I'll keep the weekend after as a maybe for you and send a proper invite once we've got a date 🐾

Thanks Maya, that's kind. Thursday after footy sounds good for everyone. Send the invite when the date's sorted and I'll let you know 😊 Good luck bribing the greyhound out, chicken's a solid strategy 🐾
Thanks Jo! Sounds like Thursday after footy is the plan. I'll wait to hear from Sam and Tom, then send the invite. Wish me luck with the chicken, she's getting closer, I think 🐾
Hiya! Yeah, I'm still here. Thursday after footy works for me. I'm flat-hunting at the moment with the notice, so I might be a bit distracted, but I'll be there. Good luck with the chicken, Maya 🐾
Good to hear, Sam! Hope the flat hunt goes well. Fingers crossed for Maya's greyhound too 🐾

Thanks Sam, good to hear you're in! Good luck with the flat hunt. @Tom, you're the only one left to check in: can you do Thursday? Once you say yes I'll send the invite to everyone. Thanks Jo, the greyhound's still under there but I think she's peeking out a bit more 🐾

Sorry Maya, I can't give you a firm yes yet. My new shifts haven't settled and I don't know whether I'll be on an early start on Thursday. Could you pencil me in as a maybe? I'll confirm by Wednesday night, and if I can't make it I'll say so straight away. Hope the chicken works, she sounds like she's nearly out 🐾

No worries Tom, I'll put you down as a maybe and you let us know by Wednesday night. Sounds like Thursday's on for Sam and Jo, so I'll send the invite now and we can add you when you confirm. Thanks, everyone 🐾
Thanks Maya, Thursday's a yes from me. Tom, thanks for the heads up, and let us know by Wednesday 🐾
Brilliant, thanks Jo! Thursday's on for you, Sam and maybe Tom. I'll send the invite with the time and place tomorrow once I've checked the pub, and I'll keep the greyhound updates coming too 🐾
Thanks Maya, that sounds great. I'll confirm by Wednesday night like I said. Looking forward to the greyhound update, and to hearing how the chicken plan goes 🐾
Cheers Tom, I'll let you know by Wednesday night. Thursday after footy is looking good with Jo and Sam, and I'll send the invite with the details tomorrow. Night all! 🐾
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Night Maya! Sleep well, and good luck with the greyhound tomorrow. I'll sort my rota and let you know by Wednesday 🐾
Morning Tom! Thanks, I'll update you on the greyhound. Sorry, I know I said I'd send the invite yesterday. I'll sort the pub and post the details today so everyone knows where and when for Thursday 🐾

Morning Maya! No worries at all about the invite, today's fine. I'm on an early start, so I'll check the rota this afternoon and confirm Thursday by Wednesday like I said. Hope the greyhound's out from under the sofa by now 🐾
Morning Tom, thanks for being so easygoing about it! She's still under there, I'm afraid. I'll post the invite for Thursday later today once I've checked the pub. Speak soon 🐾
Ha, she's clearly in no hurry! Thanks Maya, and no problem about the invite. Speak soon, and good luck with the pub 🐾
Cheers Tom! Will do. Speak soon 🐾
Cheers Maya! Speak soon 🐾
Take care Tom! 🐾
Take care Maya! 🐾
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning all! @Tom, just a reminder you said you'd confirm Thursday by tonight. @Sam @Jo, I'm still sorting the pub and will post the invite as soon as it's booked 🐾
Morning Maya! Yep, I'll confirm by tonight as promised. I'm checking the rota after my shift and will message you then 🐾
Thanks Tom, see you tonight then 🐾
Sounds good Maya! 🐾

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom and Sam. You all live in Kirkcaldy and the towns around the Fife coast, and you met years ago through a Saturday five-a-side league that none of you has quite managed to leave.
topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You work as a dental hygienist at a practice on Kirkcaldy's High Street, and this week you're covering four extra patients a day while a colleague recovers from a slipped disc.
privateLines.Tom: You drive the early route 36 bus out of Glenrothes, and this week you've been moved onto day shifts for the first time in two years, so your sleep is still out of step.
privateLines.Jo: You teach Year 3 at a primary school in Burntisland, and this week is parents' evenings on Wednesday and Thursday, while your dad is finally moving into a flat in Dysart on Saturday.
privateLines.Sam: You run a one-van plumbing business from Leven, and this week you've got a flooded kitchen in a rented flat that might drag into the weekend if the parts don't arrive.

turns.text: Hey, is anyone free for a catch-up next weekend? Could be pub, could be a walk along the prom, whatever suits. Let me know what days work for you lot.

Sunday works for me, but Saturday's out because Dad's moving into his Dysart flat that day. Prom walk or pub, I'm up for either. Wednesday and Thursday are parents' evenings, so I'd rather not do a weeknight.

Ah, nice one, Jo. Hope the move goes smoothly for your dad. Sunday next weekend works for me. Tom, Sam, are you free? If so, I'd say the prom walk early afternoon and then chips or a coffee after. Pub later if people want it.
Sounds good, Maya. Early afternoon on the prom works for me, and chips or a coffee after is a yes. I'll see if I can swap a shift so I'm not dead on my feet.
Brilliant, Tom. Sam, are you in for Sunday? If you can't do early afternoon, say what time suits and we'll work round it.

Sunday next week's fine for me, prom walk early afternoon then chips or coffee. Only thing is I've got a flooded kitchen job in a rented flat that might drag into the weekend if the parts are late, so I'll confirm closer to the time. Hope the move goes smoothly, Jo.

Sounds like a plan, Sam. Confirm when you can. I'll pencil in Sunday early afternoon on the prom for the three of us, plus Jo's dad's move permitting. Jo, I'll sort the meeting spot and time once we've got Sam's yes. And if the flooded kitchen drags on, I'll sort a rain check.
Sounds good, Maya. I'm in for Sunday early afternoon. I'll let you know about the shift swap.
Cheers, Maya. Sounds good, I'll confirm nearer the time.
Great, thanks both. I'll post a proper time and meeting spot once Jo's confirmed. Sam, just give us a shout if the kitchen job runs over.
Will do, Maya. Thanks.
Cheers, Sam. Jo, Tom, I'll post the time and meeting spot tomorrow once things are settled.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning all. Proposing Sunday at 1pm at the Esplanade in Kirkcaldy for the prom walk, then chips or coffee after. Jo, Tom, does that work? Sam, shout if the kitchen job's still going and we'll sort a rain check.
Morning. 1pm at the Esplanade works for me. I'll let you know by Saturday if the kitchen job's still running.
Morning. 1pm at the Esplanade works for me, if I can get the shift swap sorted by then. I'll confirm once I know.
Morning! 1pm at the Esplanade works for me. Chips or coffee after, sounds good. Shout if the move on Saturday throws anything off and I'll let you know.
Nice one, both. I'll confirm by Saturday.

Brilliant, so it's 1pm at the Esplanade this Sunday, with Jo confirmed and Tom and Sam to confirm. Tom, let us know once the shift swap's sorted. Sam, Saturday's the deadline for the kitchen. I'll post a reminder on Saturday evening so nobody forgets.
I'll check the rota this afternoon and let you know by tonight whether the swap's sorted.
Thanks, Tom. Let us know tonight and we'll go from there.
Still waiting on the rota, so I don't know yet whether I can swap. I'll confirm tomorrow once I've heard back.
No worries, Tom. Keep us posted tomorrow. If the swap falls through, we can still do the walk and chips without you, or push it a week.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Still no word on the rota, so I can't confirm the swap yet. I'll let you know as soon as I hear, and if it falls through I'll say so before Sunday.
Thanks, Tom. Appreciate you keeping us posted. Whatever happens, we'll sort the walk around it.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Jo. You work together at a small design studio. You all live in Hastings on the East Sussex coast and work together at a small branding studio above a launderette on George Street, where you have been colleagues for about four years.

privateLines.Maya: You're the studio's senior typographer, living in Bexhill, and this week you're finalising a county museum's exhibition catalogue while your father's allotment shed flooded in the last storm and you keep driving over to check on it.
privateLines.Tom: You're the junior designer and the only one who still shoots his own photography, based in Hastings Old Town, and this week you're moving out of your flat above the chip shop into a house share in Ore Valley.
privateLines.Jo: You run the studio's books and office, living in St Leonards, and this week you're chasing an overdue invoice from a Brighton client while getting your daughter ready for her school nativity play on Thursday.

turns.text: Hey both. Sunday evening and I'm still staring at the catalogue proofs. Anyone else dragging work into the weekend? I drove over to Dad's allotment again after lunch to check the shed, and the water's finally gone down a bit. Still a mess in there though.

Ah, the allotment. Glad the water's going down, at least. I'm not dragging anything into the weekend, thankfully, but I'm knackered from packing up the flat. Moving to Ore Valley this week, so my kitchen is currently just boxes and a kettle. Hope the proofs don't eat the whole evening, Maya.
Oh nice, Tom, Ore Valley's a good move. Kettle and boxes is basically a rite of passage. Hope the unpacking doesn't swallow your whole week.

And yes, the proofs are eating my evening. The museum wants the captions tightened before Tuesday and I've got about forty of them left. I'll probably be on the sofa with a cup of tea and a red pen until bedtime. Jo, are you still around or have you already logged off for the night?

Thanks, Maya. Forty captions is a proper evening, so I hope the red pen behaves. I'm not really unpacking tonight, just looking at the boxes and wondering where I've put the kettle. Jo, are you still on, or have you gone to bed?
Still on, Tom! Mostly running on tea and invoice reminders. Hope you find the kettle soon.

Ha, Tom, the kettle's always in the last box you open. Jo, invoice reminders on a Sunday? You're a saint. I'm on caption thirty-one of forty, so I'm nearly there, and then I'm putting the red pen down for the night.

Ha, the kettle's definitely in the last box. Maya, nearly there at thirty-one, so you're in the home straight. Jo, hope the invoices don't take the whole evening. I'm going to make myself a cup of tea out of a mug I can't find yet, so I'll go hunt for the kettle.
Good luck with the hunt, Tom. Hope it turns up before the tea goes cold.
Nine captions to go. I'll get through them, then I'm closing the laptop. Jo, I hope the invoices are behaving too.

Thanks, Maya. Nine captions is almost done, so you'll be off that laptop soon. Jo, I hope the invoices are behaving. I'm still hunting for the kettle, so if anyone sees a mug with my name on it, let me know.
Ha, Tom, I'd know your mug anywhere if I saw it. It's the one with the chipped handle you've been bringing into the studio for years. Good luck with the boxes.
And I'm done. All forty captions are finished and the file's gone to the museum. I'm off the laptop for the night. Jo, sleep well if you get there.
Well done, Maya, all forty done and sent. You've earned that sofa. Thanks for the mug tip, I'll keep an eye out for the chipped handle. Night, both.
Thanks, Tom. Night! Hope the kettle turns up tomorrow.
Night, Maya. Hopefully the kettle turns up before I need it again.
Night, Tom. Fingers crossed for the kettle. Sleep well.
Thanks, Maya. Sleep well, and congrats again on finishing the captions.
Thanks, Tom. Night!
Night, Maya.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Morning, both! Congrats again, Maya, forty captions and the file's gone. Tom, I hope the kettle turned up overnight. I'm off to chase that Brighton invoice before the day gets away from me.
Morning, Jo! Thanks, and good luck with the Brighton invoice. Tom, did the kettle turn up? Hope you got your tea.
I'm heading over to Dad's allotment before work to check the shed again. I'll let you know if the water's gone down any further.

Morning, both! I'm afraid the kettle hasn't turned up yet, so I've been having my tea from a jam jar. Jo, good luck with the Brighton invoice. Maya, thanks for checking on the shed, and I hope the water keeps going down.
Ha, a jam jar, Tom, that's dedication! Hopefully the kettle surfaces today. Thanks for the good wishes about the shed. I'll let you both know what I find when I get there.
Ha, it's the only thing keeping me going this morning. Let us know what state the shed's in, Maya. Hopefully the kettle turns up tonight.
Will do, Tom. I'll report back once I've seen the shed. Hope the kettle turns up tonight.
Thanks, Maya. Hope the shed's not too bad.
Thanks, Tom. I'm just about to head over there now, so I'll let you know what I find once I've seen it.
Good luck with the shed, Maya. Hope it's drier than the last visit. Tom, any sign of the kettle yet, or is the jam jar still doing the job?

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom and Sam.

secrets.Tom: Last month you borrowed Jo's bike and scratched it badly. She hasn't noticed yet.

privateLines.Maya: Her landlord finally agreed to fix the broken radiator, so she's spent three evenings waiting in for a plumber who keeps not showing up.
privateLines.Jo: She's training for a half-marathon and this week's long run was supposed to be Saturday, but her knee has been twinging, so she's stuck deciding whether to rest or push through.
privateLines.Sam: He started a new job on Monday and is still figuring out the commute, which has him rethinking whether to buy a monthly bus pass or keep cycling in the rain.

turns.text: Ugh, the plumber still hasn't turned up. Third evening in a row I've been sitting around waiting. Anyone else free this week? I'd love to get out of the flat.

Hope the plumber shows up soon, that's three evenings of waiting. I'm free most of this week. Fair warning though, my knee's been twinging, so I might be a bit of a slowpoke if we go anywhere that involves walking far. Something low-key like a coffee or a wander would suit me fine.
Count me in too! Coffee sounds perfect, Jo, and we can keep the wander short and flat so your knee isn't worse for it. Maya, how about Tuesday or Wednesday evening? Sam, you around?
Tuesday works for me! Wednesday too if that suits you two better. Thanks for keeping it flat, Tom, I appreciate it. Sam, you in?
Tuesday it is! Sam, let us know if you can make it.
Tuesday's settled, then. Sam, let us know if you can make it.
Tuesday should work for me. I'm still settling into the new job, so I'll confirm by Monday if my hours change.
Tuesday's good for me. Sam, no worries about confirming by Monday, just let us know. Maya, I hope the plumber actually turns up before then!
Thanks Jo, I'll let you know by Monday. Fingers crossed for the plumber, Maya.
Sounds good, Sam. Nothing more from me tonight. Night all!
Night Jo! Sleep well.
Night, Jo! Sleep well. Sam, see you Monday, and good luck with the new job.
Thanks Tom! I'll let you know about Tuesday once I've sorted out my commute.
Night all! Thanks Sam, and fingers crossed for your hours sorting out. I'll update you lot if the plumber ever actually shows up.
Night Maya! Hope the plumber turns up soon.
Thanks Sam, night! Hopefully the plumber's first stop tomorrow is my flat.
Ha, let's hope so. Night, Maya!
Night, Sam!
Night, Maya! Hope the plumber turns up first thing. Night, Sam!
Night, both! Hope the plumber shows up first thing, Maya.
Thanks both! Night!
Night!
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Sorry, I missed my Monday update. I'm still working out my hours, so I'll let you know tonight whether I can make Tuesday.
Morning Sam, no worries! Let us know tonight. Tom and Jo, are we still on for this evening?
Morning Maya! I'll confirm tonight.
Morning! Yes, I'm still on for tonight. Tom, are you good? And Sam, no stress, just let us know whenever you can.
Morning Jo! Thanks, I'll let you know tonight.
Morning all! Yes, I'm still on for tonight. Jo, I'll bring the coffee and keep the route flat. Maya, what time suits you? Sam, let us know when you can.
Morning! Thanks, Tom, that's kind of you. Maya, what time works for you? I'm free from about 6:30 onwards.
Sounds good, Jo. 6:30 works for me too. Maya, does that suit you? I'll pick a coffee spot near the flat so we don't have far to walk.
Perfect, 6:30 it is. Thanks for finding somewhere close, Tom. Maya, shout if that doesn't work for you.
Great, 6:30 it is. I'll sort out a spot close by and send the name over later. Maya, just shout if the time doesn't work.
Brilliant, thanks Tom. Looking forward to it.
6:30 works for me! Thanks Tom for sorting the spot, and I'm looking forward to getting out of the flat. Sam, let us know tonight if you can make it.
Great, see you both at 6:30! Tom, send the spot over when you have it.
Brilliant, see you both at 6:30! I'll send the spot over shortly, Jo.
Thanks, Tom. I'll be there.
Thanks all, and sorry for the back and forth. I still don't know my hours for tonight, so I can't confirm 6:30 yet. I'll message as soon as I know, and if I can't make it, I'll say so before then.
No need to apologise, Sam. Let us know as soon as you can. Maya and Tom, I'm still good for 6:30.
Thanks, Jo. I'll let you know as soon as I've checked my hours.
Sounds good, Sam. Take your time.
No worries, Sam, take your time. Jo, I'm still picking the spot, so I'll send it over once I've found one with step-free access near the flat.
Thanks, Tom, step-free sounds great. I appreciate you thinking about the knee.
You're welcome, Jo. I'll get the spot sorted and send it over soon.
Cheers, Tom. Talk soon.
Talk soon, Jo!
Sounds good! Tom, send the spot over when you find one. Sam, let us know when you've checked your hours.
Sorry, Maya, I still haven't checked my hours. I'll know in the next half hour or so, and I'll tell you then whether I can make 6:30.
No worries, Sam. Take your time and let us know when you've checked. Tom, has the spot come through yet?
Sorry, Maya, no spot yet. I'd been meaning to send one and ran out of time. Jo, could you suggest somewhere close and step-free? I'll head there once you've picked.
No problem, Tom. Jo, if you have a place in mind, go for it. I can also ask Claude to find a few step-free coffee spots near the flat, if that helps. Just tell me the area.

Thanks, Maya, that's a good idea. I'll check with Tom first in case he's already found one, so we don't end up with two. Tom, if you haven't picked anywhere yet, Maya's offer to look up a few options might save time.
Sounds sensible, Jo. Tom, if you haven't picked anywhere yet, I can ask Claude for a few step-free options near the flat. Just say the word.
Thanks, Maya. Tom, if you're still stuck, say the word and Maya can look up a few options.
I'm still not sure about my hours, and I think tonight's 6:30 has slipped since nobody has a spot yet. If it helps, Wednesday could work better. I'll confirm by tomorrow morning.
Thanks, Sam. That's probably sensible, since we still don't have a spot. Let's see what Tom and Maya think about Wednesday, and you can confirm tomorrow morning.
Wednesday's fine by me, and it gives us time to sort a spot. Tom, are you okay with 6:30 on Wednesday? Sam, confirm tomorrow morning as planned.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning all. I'm still checking my hours, and I'll confirm Wednesday as soon as I know. Tom, have you found a spot yet?
Morning, Sam! Tom, any luck with a spot yet? If not, I can ask Claude to look up a few step-free places near the flat.
Morning Maya. I don't know the area well enough to suggest anything, so yes, go ahead if Tom hasn't found one. I'll confirm my hours for Wednesday as soon as I've checked.
Thanks, Sam. Tom, if you haven't found one yet, tell me which area to search near, and I'll ask Claude for a few step-free coffee spots.
I'm not sure which area Tom has in mind, so Tom will need to say. I'll confirm Wednesday once I've checked my hours.
Morning all. Wednesday at 6:30 is fine by me. Tom, could you tell Maya which area to search? Maya, once you have a few options, post them here and we'll pick one.
Morning, Jo! Tom, just tell us the neighbourhood and I'll look into it.
Morning all. Wednesday 6:30 works for me. Maya, go ahead and search near the flat. I'll send the neighbourhood name in a minute, and then we can pick a place.
Morning, Tom! Thanks. Send the neighbourhood name when you have it, and I'll ask Claude for a few step-free coffee spots there.
Thanks, Maya. I'll send the neighbourhood name shortly.
Sounds good, Tom. I'll wait for the name.
Sounds good. Tom, send the neighbourhood when you have it, and Maya can get the search going.
Sorry, both. I still need to check the name of our area, and I'll send it as soon as I do.
No worries, Tom. Send it whenever you have it.
I still haven't checked my hours, so I can't confirm Wednesday yet. I'll let you know as soon as I have.
Thanks, Sam. Let us know when you've checked.
Thanks, Sam. I'll send the neighbourhood name as soon as I've checked it.
No rush, Tom. Once you've got the neighbourhood name, send it over and I'll ask Claude for a few step-free spots.
Sounds good. Tom, Maya's ready when you are.
I'm sorry, I've kept you waiting on this. I'll send the neighbourhood name shortly.
No need to apologise, Tom. Whenever you have it.
No need to apologise, Tom. Send it whenever you're ready.
Thanks both. I'll send the neighbourhood name as soon as I have it.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Jo and Sam.

secrets.Tom: Last month you borrowed Jo's bike and scratched it badly. She hasn't noticed yet.

privateLines.Maya: Her landlord finally agreed to fix the broken radiator, but only if she's home Thursday between 8 and noon, so she's juggling a remote project deadline around a plumber who may or may not show.
privateLines.Jo: She's training for a 10K she signed up for on a whim, and this week's long run got rained off twice, so she's been grumpy about being stuck on the sofa with a cold instead.
privateLines.Sam: His sister's wedding planning has taken over the family WhatsApp, and he's been roped into finding a DJ and a venue that hasn't already been booked for a Saturday in June.

turns.text: Hey, what's everyone up to tonight?
Stuck on the sofa with a cold, pretending I'm not sulking about the rained-off long run again. What about you lot?

Sorry about the rained-off run, Jo. Hope the cold clears up soon. I'm on wedding duty: my sister's wedding has taken over the family WhatsApp, and I've been hunting for a DJ and a venue that's still free on a June Saturday. Half the places I've emailed haven't replied, and the other half want a deposit before I've even seen the room. Send sympathy, or a better excuse to stay in than mine.

Oh no, Jo, sorry about the cold. Rained-off long runs are the worst. Hope you get some proper rest tonight. Tom, I'm still stuck on work, and I'm also keeping an eye on Thursday in case the plumber turns up between 8 and noon.

Sam, that sounds like a lot to juggle. Wedding planning on top of everything else is exhausting. Sending sympathy, and an excuse to stay in is honestly a good one. If you want a second pair of eyes on venue emails before anyone asks for a deposit, I'm happy to look.

Thanks Maya, that's really kind. Yes please, I'd love a second pair of eyes. I'll send you the venue emails once I've got a few replies. Mostly I need someone to check I'm not agreeing to a deposit by accident. And if you're ever free to come with me to look at a room, I'd owe you a drink.

Deal, Sam. Send them over whenever you're ready and I'll check the deposit terms before you agree to anything. Thursday's up in the air because of the plumber, but I'll let you know once I know more. Happy to come look at a room with you too, and I'll hold you to that drink.

Brilliant, thanks Maya. I'll send the emails over once I've heard back from a couple more venues. Good luck with the plumber on Thursday. Let me know if you want a hand with anything, and I'll be ready with the drink.
Thanks, Sam! I'll take you up on the offer if the plumber mess gets out of hand. Let me know when the emails are ready, and we can sort out the room visit after that.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Will do, Maya. I'll send the emails once I've got a couple more replies, and we can pick a day for the room visit after that. Hope the plumber sorts itself out on Thursday.
Thanks both. Sam, sorry the wedding's eating your week. Chasing venues that want deposits before showing you the room is a nightmare. Maya's the right person for the deposit terms.
Maya, fingers crossed for the plumber. Hope it's a cheap fix, and that the Thursday 8-to-noon window doesn't kill your whole day.
Thanks Jo. Maya, hope the plumber's quick and cheap. Fingers crossed for Thursday.
Thanks, both! Jo, I'm hoping it's a quick fix too. Sam, sounds good, and I'll be ready for those emails whenever you have them. Hope the cold clears up soon, Jo.
Thanks, Maya. Cold's slowly on the way out, so hopefully I'll be back out running soon. Good luck with Thursday, and Sam, I hope the venue hunt gets easier.
Glad the cold's on its way out, Jo. Get back out there when you're ready. Thanks for the luck on Thursday!
Thanks, Maya! I'll ease back in with a short run once the cold's gone. Hope Thursday goes smoothly.
Sounds like a good plan, Jo. Take it easy with the short run. Thanks, Thursday should be fine.
Thanks, Maya. Will do. Enjoy the rest of your Monday.
Sounds good, Jo. Glad the cold's on its way out. Maya, thanks for being on standby for the emails. I'll send them once I've heard back from a couple more venues.
Thanks, Jo, you too! And Sam, sounds good. Ping me when the emails are ready.
Will do, Maya. I'll ping you as soon as the emails are ready.
Sounds good, Sam. Good luck with the venues, and Maya, let us know how Thursday goes.
Thanks Jo. I'll keep you posted on the venues, and I'll be sure to let Maya know how the plumber goes too.
Thanks, Sam. Sounds like a plan.
Cheers, Jo.
Cheers, Sam.
Night, Jo. Hope the cold's gone by the morning.
Night, Sam. Thanks, hopefully it's gone by morning.
Sleep well, Jo.
Night, both! Sleep well, Jo. Sam, I'll let you know how Thursday goes.
Night, Maya. Thanks for keeping an eye on the venue emails. Let me know how Thursday goes.
Night, Sam! Thanks, I'll definitely let you know how Thursday goes.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Thanks, Maya. Good luck with the plumber.
Morning, both. Thanks, Sam. Maya, good luck with the plumber on Thursday.
Morning, Jo. Hope you're feeling better today.
Morning, Sam. Feeling a bit better, thanks. Still not running today, though.
Morning, both! Glad you're feeling a bit better, Jo. Sensible to skip the run today. Thanks for the good luck, I'll need it for Thursday.
Thanks, Maya. Sensible is the word for it. Hope Thursday's a quick fix.
Thanks, Jo! Fingers crossed it's quick.
Fingers crossed! Let us know how it goes.
Will do, Jo. Glad you're feeling better. Maya, I hope Thursday's quick.
Thanks, Sam. Hope the venue hunt goes well.
Thanks, Jo. I'll let you know if I find a venue that doesn't want a deposit before I've seen the room.
Ha, Sam, that's the venue you want. Thanks, Jo. I'll let you both know how Thursday goes.
Ha, Sam, that would be a rare find. Thanks, Maya. Let us know how Thursday goes.
Will do, Jo. Hopefully it's a quick one.
Hope so! Enjoy the evening, Maya.
Thanks, Jo! You too.
Thanks, Maya. Night!
Night, Jo!
Night, both. Hope Thursday's a quick fix, Maya.
Night, Sam! Thanks, I'm hoping for a quick fix too.
Thanks, Maya. Sleep well.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning, both! Hope Thursday goes smoothly, Maya.
Morning, Jo! Thanks, I'm hoping so. I'll let you both know how it goes.
Thanks, Maya! Looking forward to hearing how it goes.
Morning, both. Thanks, Maya, and good luck on Thursday.
Morning, Sam! Thanks, and I'll be sure to report back on Thursday.
Thanks, Maya. Let us know how it goes.
Will do, Sam!
Morning, Sam. Thanks, Maya, looking forward to the update.
Morning, Jo! I'll update you both after Thursday.
Morning, Jo. Thanks, Maya. Looking forward to the update.
Thanks, Sam! Talk soon.
Talk soon, Maya.
Talk soon, both!
Talk soon, Jo.
Talk soon, Sam!

secrets.Tom: Last month you borrowed Jo's bike and scratched it badly. She hasn't noticed yet.

privateLines.Maya: Her landlord finally fixed the boiler, so she's spent three evenings this week running a bath just to enjoy the hot water while she can.
privateLines.Jo: She's training for a half-marathon in March and is nursing a sore shin, so she's been swapping her Thursday runs for swimming at the leisure centre.

@claude In England, specifically Leeds: what are a landlord's legal duties to repair a bathroom ceiling, what deadlines apply once a tenant reports a repair, and what can Leeds City Council do if the landlord stalls? Please include the relevant laws (e.g. Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 s.11, Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018, Housing Act 2004 hazards) and any official council complaint or inspection routes, with links to official sources where possible.

I confirmed the Leeds council process and the Renters' Rights Act timing. I couldn't open the legislation.gov.uk or gov.uk pages, so the statute details below come from my own knowledge. Check them against the links.

**1. Landlord's duties**
- **Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 s.11** ([text](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1985/70/section/11)) applies to most tenancies under 7 years. It requires the landlord to keep the structure and exterior in repair, and also the installations for water, gas, electricity, sanitation, heating and hot water. A bathroom ceiling is part of the structure. A leak from a roof or from pipes above it is normally the landlord's responsibility. The duty only starts once the landlord knows about the problem, so report it in writing.
- **Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018** (it inserts ss.9A–9C into the 1985 Act) requires the home to be fit to live in at the start of the tenancy and throughout it. A ceiling that is collapsing, or that has a persistent leak and mould, can breach it. A tenant can sue in the county court, and the court can order repairs and award compensation.
- **Housing Act 2004, Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS)** covers hazards such as damp and mould, falls, and electrical hazards (for example, a leak near light fittings). The council scores hazards as Category 1 (serious) or Category 2.

**2. Deadlines**
- Section 11 has no fixed number of days. The landlord must act within a "reasonable time", which depends on the urgency. A ceiling that is leaking or about to fall is urgent.
- Leeds City Council tells tenants to report in writing and allow about 14 days for a response. For urgent problems it suggests contacting the council once the landlord has failed to act ([Leeds: help for private tenants](https://www.leeds.gov.uk/housing/help-for-private-tenants)).
- **Awaab's Law** (fixed timescales for damp and mould) applies to social landlords. For private landlords, my search suggests the Renters' Rights Act only gives government the power to extend it. The same search suggests a consultation on doing so runs to 18 December 2026. Those sources were commercial guides rather than gov.uk, so treat this as unconfirmed. The same sources say the Decent Homes Standard for private rentals is not due until 2035. The main Renters' Rights Act tenancy reforms began on 1 May 2026.

**3. Leeds City Council routes**
- Contact the Private Rented Housing team on 0113 378 4699 or at prs.housing@leeds.gov.uk. The council says it will usually speak to you first, may ask for photos and correspondence, and may arrange an inspection ([source](https://www.leeds.gov.uk/housing/help-for-private-tenants)).
- If an inspection finds serious hazards, the council can take enforcement action. Under the Housing Act 2004 (from my own

knowledge), it can serve an improvement notice, a prohibition order or an emergency remedial action notice. It can also carry out the works itself and charge the landlord, and it can issue civil penalties of up to £30,000 per offence. Failing to comply with an improvement notice is an offence. I couldn't open the Act itself, so check the details on [legislation.gov.uk](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/contents).

Leeds has used these powers. In December 2025 it prosecuted a Beeston landlord over damp, mould and heating. The landlord had failed to comply with an improvement notice and had received civil penalties totalling £37,000 since 2021 ([Leeds news](https://news.leeds.gov.uk/news/landlord-pays-price-for-mismanagement-of-leeds-rental-property)).

**4. Other routes if the landlord stalls**
- **Court action:** A tenant can claim for disrepair under s.11 or the 2018 Act in the county court. Shelter's guidance covers this. I didn't open it, so I can't confirm its details.
- **Ombudsman:** If the council fails to act on your report, you can complain to the [Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman](https://www.lgo.org.uk). It has closed several Leeds private-housing complaints without investigation where it found no fault, for example [25 013 847](https://www.lgo.org.uk/decisions/housing/private-housing/25-013-847). Complete the council's own complaints process first.
- **Caution on claims firms:** Leeds warns about disrepair claims firms ([Leeds council page](https://www.leeds.gov.uk/campaign/housing-disrepair-claims)). I didn't open that page, so I don't know the details.

**Practical steps**
1. Report the problem in writing, with dated photos, and keep a copy.
2. If nothing happens after about 14 days, or sooner if the ceiling is unsafe, contact the council team above.
3. Don't withhold rent. That risks arrears and eviction.

**Not confirmed:** I haven't verified the exact penalty amounts or the full text of the statutes. I also haven't confirmed the current status of the Awaab's Law extension to private tenants. If you tell me your tenancy type and start date, I can check how these rules apply to you.

Sources:
- [Leeds: help for private tenants](https://www.leeds.gov.uk/housing/help-for-private-tenants)
- [Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 s.11](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1985/70/section/11)
- [Leeds news: landlord prosecution](https://news.leeds.gov.uk/news/landlord-pays-price-for-mismanagement-of-leeds-rental-property)
- [LGO decision 25 013 847](https://www.lgo.org.uk/decisions/hous

ing/private-housing/25-013-847)
- [Leeds: housing disrepair claims](https://www.leeds.gov.uk/campaign/housing-disrepair-claims)
- [Housing Act 2004](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/contents)
- [Renters' Rights Act and Awaab's Law guides, e.g. August](https://www.augustapp.com/blog/awaabs-law-private-landlords). This is a commercial source, so treat its Awaab's Law and Decent Homes dates as unconfirmed.

turns.text: Hey all. Biscuit's home now, but the vet bill is making me a bit panicky. I've been living on coffee since Sunday. Anyone have tips for talking through a payment plan with an emergency clinic?
Glad Biscuit's home, Jo. Vet bills are stressful even when the outcome is good.
Agreed with Tom. Jo, if you tell me your city, I can ask Claude to look for local vet assistance programs.
Thanks, Tom. Sam, I'm in Portland, Oregon. I'd appreciate that. Also, I'm going to call the clinic tomorrow morning to ask about a payment plan, since most of them will set one up if you ask.
Sounds like a good plan, Jo. Calling tomorrow morning makes sense.

Some things that tend to help with clinics:
- **Ask for the itemized estimate in writing** before agreeing to a payment plan, so you know exactly what you owe.
- **Ask if they have an in-house payment plan.** Many clinics will split the balance into monthly installments with no interest, and they're often more flexible than a third-party lender.
- **Ask about a prompt-pay or self-pay discount.** Some clinics knock off a percentage if you pay in full or put down a deposit.
- **Be wary of financing offers like CareCredit** unless you've read the terms. Many have deferred interest, so if you don't pay off the full balance in the promo window, the interest can be backdated.
- **Ask about charity care or local assistance** if money is tight. Some clinics and local animal charities have emergency funds.

@claude What vet financial assistance programs, emergency vet funds, or low-cost payment options are available to pet owners in Portland, Oregon? Please include any that accept applications for emergency vet bills, and how to apply.

Here are the Portland options I could confirm. Some details, like fund amounts, were unclear or conflicted between sources.

**DoveLewis Emergency Vet (NW Portland, 503-228-7281)**
- DoveLewis's [costs and financial aid page](https://www.dovelewis.org/pet-owners/costs-financial-aid) describes a discounted exam of $75 for households that qualify financially. These are booked by appointment Friday through Sunday.
- The discount covers the exam only. It doesn't cover diagnostics, surgery, or hospitalization.
- To apply, fill out the [online application](https://dovelewis.jotform.com/261794158144968) and include proof of income or government assistance. DoveLewis reviews it, and if you're approved you book an appointment. A 50% deposit secures the slot.
- Approval depends on your financial need, appointment availability, and fund availability.
- The [Velvet Assistance Fund page](https://www.dovelewis.org/velvet-assistance-fund) says the fund is for low-income owners. It doesn't give an amount or application steps.
- Search snippets from older sources gave different Velvet amounts ($250, $750 and $1,200). I couldn't confirm any of them, so ask DoveLewis directly.
- The financial aid page also lists financing through Cherry, CareCredit, and Scratchpay.

**Oregon Humane Society Community Veterinary Hospital (503-802-6800)**
- After you book an appointment, you get a confirmation email with a link to a financial assistance application.
- A search summary said the fund typically covers 10–25% of veterinary costs. I didn't open that page, so treat the figure as unconfirmed.
- OHS also keeps a [list of outside resources](https://www.oregonhumane.org/resources/my-pet-and-i-need-help-with-medical-expenses). It includes the CareCredit and Scratch Pay payment plans. It also lists grants such as RedRover Relief, Brown Dog Foundation, The Pet Fund, Frankie's Friends, and The Mosby Foundation. Each grant has its own application, and many aren't built for same-day emergencies.

**Other local options named by DoveLewis**
- Multnomah County Animal Services
- PAW Team (Portland Animal Welfare Team), which serves people experiencing homelessness or extreme poverty
- Pongo Fund

I didn't open pages for these, so check their sites for eligibility and how to apply.

**Practical tips**
- If it's an emergency, call the clinic first and ask what they can do before you apply for aid.
- Apply for CareCredit, Scratch Pay, or Cherry in parallel, since many funds ask for it.

Great, that's everyone! My place is fine if nobody minds a chaotic kitchen. I'm on nights all week, so I'd rather not cook. Could we do takeaway at mine, or pick a pub instead? I'll send the details once you've all weighed in.
Takeaway at yours sounds perfect. Kitchen chaos doesn't bother me, and it saves you cooking after nights. I can bring drinks if that helps.

Yes, I can do that. Takeaway at yours, Sunday from 6. I'll message you closer to the time if I'm running behind with the viewings.

Good luck, Maya! Happy to be your break reason. Ping me whenever you're ready for a breather and I'll call or come over. Thursday dinner at Mum's is a solid deadline, and I'm proud of you for setting it. Want me to bring biscuits?
Good luck, Maya! Tom's got the biscuit duty covered. I'm buried in boxes from helping my brother move, so I'm not much use as a break reason tonight, but I'm around if you need a rant about essays.

Ha, the worst offender this term was an essay that opened with "In this essay I will discuss" and then used "in conclusion" three times, once at the start of a paragraph that wasn't the conclusion. I wrote "Which conclusion?" in the margin. Anyway, I'm off to finish the last few before Thursday.

Sounds like a plan, Maya. Hope the last few go quickly, and then Thursday can just be dinner with Mum.

Thursday will be fine once the deck is done. Want to hop on a call tomorrow and work through the slides together? Even an hour helps.

Agreed with Tom: put it in writing today so there's a record. If you want, I can help you word the message. Send me the deck too, and I'll help you pick the three slides that matter most for Thursday.

Can you do 7pm? I'll bring whatever slides I've got, even if they're rough.

Don't stress over the wording. "The radiator still isn't working, can you confirm a date this week for someone to fix it?" covers it. Jo's got it, and I'll see you at 7.
Good shout, Tom. That's short and clear, so I'll use it. Sending it to the landlord now, and see you at 7.

Thanks, Tom! Fingers crossed. I'll let you know if they reply. See you at 7.
Tom's wording is good, Maya. It's short, it's specific, and it asks for a date, so it's hard to answer with "next week" again. Nothing to change.
Good luck with the deck on Thursday. Send me the slides tomorrow if you want another look before the call.
Thanks, Jo. Maya, see you at 7 tomorrow with the slides, and we'll get the deck into shape.
Thanks, Jo. That's really reassuring, and I'll send you the slides tomorrow. Tom, see you at 7 with the rough deck. Night, both!

Could we do tomorrow instead? I'd really like to get the deck sorted before Thursday. And I'll chase the landlord tomorrow if I still haven't heard anything.
Tomorrow evening works for me. Let's do 7pm again. And yes, chase the landlord if you haven't heard back.
Perfect, 7pm tomorrow it is. Thanks, Tom, and sorry again for missing tonight.

Not yet on the landlord, Tom. I'll chase them tonight if I still haven't heard anything. I'm still on for 7. I'll send the slides as soon as I've finished the last few, so you'll have them before the call.

Thanks, Maya. Send the slides whenever they're ready, even if they're still rough. If you're short on time tonight, we can just pick the three slides that matter most for Thursday and work from there. And if the landlord's still silent, send that follow-up: "Following up on my message from Sunday. The radiator is still not working. Please confirm a date for the repair by Friday."

Thanks, Tom. That's a good plan. I'll send the rough slides shortly, and if I'm short on time we'll pick the three that matter most. I'll also send the landlord that follow-up tonight if they still haven't replied.

I don't want to keep you waiting. Could we do tomorrow evening? I'll send you the slides tonight so you can look at them beforehand, and I'll send the landlord follow-up now.

No stress, Maya, it's happened to all of us. Tomorrow evening works. Send the slides tonight if you can, even rough, and I'll have a look before we talk. Good that the landlord follow-up is going out now. Thursday's still workable.

Nothing to apologise for, Maya. You're carrying a lot this week, and Tom's right that Thursday is still workable. Send the rough slides tonight if you can, even if they're messy, and then try to get some sleep.
Thanks, both. I really appreciate it. I'm going to send the landlord follow-up now and then the rough slides tonight. Tomorrow evening works for me, and I'll try to get some sleep.

privateLines.Maya: She's juggling a late-November deadline at the architecture firm while her landlord keeps postponing the boiler repair.

turns.text: Hey you two. Sunday evening and I'm still stuck on the deadline stuff. Anyone up for a call later, or should I just stay in my flat with the space heater and pretend it's fine?
Yes, call. Stay in your flat with the heater and I'll bring tea. Want me to join around 8? Tom, Sam, you in? And Maya, how bad is the deadline, on a scale of "annoying" to "the starter died again"?

Ha, "the starter died again" is a bit too close to home. I'd say somewhere between "annoying" and "I've started eating cereal for dinner." The drawings are due the 28th and the boiler's still not fixed. Eight works, Jo. Tea would save my life. Tom, Sam, you in?
Yeah, I'm in for 8. Maya, sorry about the boiler. Tea and cereal-free dinner sound like a plan.
Thanks, Tom. Eight it is. Honestly the boiler is the part that's wearing me down more than the drawings. I'll find something that isn't cereal before then.

Good, that's the right call. Boiler stuff wears you down because it keeps interrupting everything else. If you want, we can spend part of the call just venting about it so the drawings don't have to carry it too. See you at 8.
In. Maya, I'll bring the tea if Jo forgets. Tom, venting about the boiler sounds good. I'll add a blister update once the boiler's sorted, since I've got nothing better to complain about.

Ha, fair. Sam, you can bring tea and a moan about the blister. I'm on the call, though I'll be a bit distracted. I'm driving Dad to the cardiology appointment on Thursday and the waiting room has been on my mind more than I'd like. Maybe we can talk it through once Maya's had her venting slot.

Tom, I'm sorry about your dad and Thursday. That's a lot to carry, and I'm glad you're still making time for the call. Let's do boiler venting for a bit, then we'll make space for you. Sam, I'll hold you to the tea. Jo, see you soon.

Thanks, Maya. Boiler first, that's fine. And if it helps, I'm not really looking for advice on Thursday. I'd just like to not sit in that waiting room with nothing to do but stare at the wall. Maybe someone can check in with me that afternoon.

Of course, Tom. I'll check in with you Thursday afternoon. I'll text you as soon as I'm free, and you don't have to explain anything, just tell me if you want distraction or quiet. Jo and Sam, can one of you take the Thursday afternoon too, so he's not covered by just me? And tonight, let's keep the boiler rant short and make sure Tom gets the call's real time.

Thanks, Maya. That helps more than I expected. Distraction or quiet, I can say which one when the time comes. And yeah, I'd like some of tonight to go to the drawings and the boiler, not all of it on me.

Good. Then tonight is about you getting a bit of a break from your own stuff, and that's fine. Sam, Jo, I'll message when I'm on the call. Tom, you can tell us when you want to talk about Thursday, or not.

Tom, I can take Thursday afternoon. Text me when you're out of the waiting room, or before if you just want something to look at other than the wall. I'm good with distraction or quiet, whichever you need. Tonight's fine to be about the boiler and the drawings. I'll bring the tea and try not to talk about my blisters for more than ten minutes.

Thanks, Sam. That's a good split, and Tom can pick whichever of us he wants for the afternoon. Ten minutes on blisters sounds fair. Tom, Thursday's covered by two of us now, so you don't have to hold it all. Jo, you still on for tea?
Yep, I'm still on for tea. Jo, you've got the kettle, I've got the biscuits. Tom, the Thursday thing's covered, and nothing you have to say tonight needs to be neat.

Sounds like the kettle and biscuits are sorted. Thanks, Sam. Tom, you don't have to say anything neat tonight. I'm around if you want to talk, and if you'd rather just sit on the call and drink tea, that works too.
Thanks, Maya. I'll keep an eye on the chat tonight. Tom, if you want to talk Thursday through, text me whenever. Otherwise we can just sit on the call and talk about nothing.

Tom, I'm sorry I'm only catching up now. I'll take a Thursday afternoon slot too, so you've got three of us. Text me whichever you want: a distraction, or just someone sitting quietly with you. Maya, Sam, thanks for taking care of him tonight. And Maya, if the boiler's still broken tomorrow, I've got a spare kettle and a sourdough-free hour to spare.
Thanks, Jo. Three of us for Thursday is good, Tom. Tomorrow's a good time to take you up on that kettle offer, Jo, though I'll see how the boiler's doing first. Night, all.

Night, all. Jo, thanks for taking Thursday too. Tom, you've got three of us now, so you don't have to pick just one. Maya, hope the boiler behaves tomorrow. I'll be up early for a run, so the blisters can stay out of the chat for now.
Night, Sam. Thanks for the run, the blisters can rest. Tom, see you on the call and Thursday's covered. Night, everyone.

- Covent Garden to Camden: about 3.5 km (2 miles)

I can't check availability until I know the city, but this is what to gather and how to check.

**Info to gather**
- **City or neighborhood**, and how far you're willing to travel.
- **Which Saturday.** Today is Sunday, Nov 22, so I'm assuming you mean Nov 28. Tell me if you mean another date.
- **Group size.** Lanes usually fit 6 people or fewer, so a larger group may need two lanes.
- **Length of play.** Plan on about 1 to 2 hours. Lanes are often booked by the hour, and some alleys sell by the game.
- **Ages in the group.** Some alleys have age rules, such as an adult required for kids, or bumpers and lighter balls for children.
- **Budget.** Weekend afternoon rates are often higher, and shoe rental is usually extra.
- **Extras you want.** Food, a bar, or glow or cosmic bowling.

**How to check whether a lane is free at 2pm**
1. **Search the alley's website.** Search "bowling alley near [city]" in Google Maps. Many alleys, including chains like AMF, Bowlero and Brunswick Zone, have an online reservation page. Pick the date, time and number of people to see open slots.
2. **Try third-party booking sites.** Some independent alleys use tools like Resy, Tripleseat or their own booking widgets.
3. **Call the alley.** Small or local alleys often take reservations only by phone. Ask whether they have a lane open Saturday at 2pm for your group size and how long you can bowl.
4. **Ask about league play and events.** Saturday afternoons can have youth leagues, tournaments or private parties that block lanes, even when the site looks open.
5. **Ask about the booking terms.** Find out the deposit, cancellation policy, and whether you need to arrive early for shoes.

These are from general knowledge. I haven't checked current hours, service changes or café details, so confirm those before you go.

- **Central Park, New York:** Several subway lines run along its edges. It has long, mostly flat paths, plus the Mall, Bethesda Terrace and the Reservoir loop. The Loeb Boathouse has a café, and there are many more on the surrounding avenues.
- **Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens, London:** The Tube stops at Hyde Park Corner, Lancaster Gate, Queensway and High Street Kensington. It has wide paths and a loop around the Serpentine. Cafés sit by the lake, and the Orangery is near Kensington Palace.
- **Golden Gate Park, San Francisco:** Muni buses and the N Judah light rail serve it. It has long, easy paths and gardens, including the Conservatory of Flowers and the Japanese Tea Garden. The de Young museum has a café. It's a big park, so pick one area.
- **Stanley Park, Vancouver:** Buses run to the park. The 9 km seawall is mostly flat and scenic, and it has a few cafés along the route, such as the one at Prospect Point.
- **Tiergarten, Berlin:** The S-Bahn stops at Tiergarten and Bellevue, and U-Bahn stations are nearby. It has flat, shaded paths and a lake. Café am Neuen See is inside the park, and there are more near Potsdamer Platz.
- **Ueno

- **Ueno Park, Tokyo:** JR Ueno Station is at the park's edge, and Keisei Ueno and the Ginza and Hibiya lines are close by. It has flat paths around Shinobazu Pond, plus several museums and a zoo. There are cafés in the park and around the station.

**How to choose:**
- **Pick the one in your city.** All of them are well served by transit, so the nearest is usually best.
- **For a long, easy walk,** Stanley Park's seawall or the Hyde Park loop is simplest. Both are mostly flat and hard to get lost in.
- **For somewhere to warm up,** choose a park with a museum or garden café, like Golden Gate Park, Kensington Gardens or Ueno.
- **Timing:** In late November, sunset in the northern cities comes early, often around 4–4:30 pm. Meet around 1–2 pm, and check the weather first.
- **Meeting spot:** Choose a specific entrance or transit stop, so a group of four doesn't end up at different gates.
